results.title: Tokyo Shibuya Don Quijote Shopping Review! Japan Travel Vlog / What to Buy
results.content:
[0:48] We will go to Don Quijote from Hachiko Gate, which many people use in Shibuya Station.
[0:55] It takes about 5 minutes on foot to the destination.
[0:59] When you see Shibuya 109, make a right turn.  After about a minute's walk, a signboard will come into view.
[1:08] This is the MEGA Don Quijote Shibuya flagship store introduced this time. [...] [1:14] Unlike regular Don Quijote stores, this Don Quijote has the word "MEGA" on it and is a large Don Quijote that carries a wide variety of products.
[1:25] The store is open 24 hours a day, every day of the week.
[1:30] The store is a large building with two basement floors and seven floors above ground, selling about 80,000 different items.
[1:39] The seventh floor is for international tourists and is especially recommended for viewers of this channel. [...] [11:44] Don Quijote's electrical appliances are reasonably priced so many Japanese people come here to buy them.
[11:52] Stationery is also sold on this floor and erasers are especially popular.
[11:58] These erasers are made in the image of Japanese bread and the packaging is well reproduced.
[12:06] The erasers in the packaging are shaped like a cute bread and smells like butter and vanilla.
[12:12] The erasers are cute but they can also erase letters well. It's a perfect souvenir for kids.

You have reached the finish line. This floor is perfect for last-minute souvenir shopping and for handling your tax-free procedures. If you need a new suitcase for everything you picked up along the way, you can find one here as well.  
   
 Main Products  
 ・Suitcases (carry cases)

MEGA Don Quijote Shibuya Main Store 7F

MEGA Don Quijote Shibuya Main Store 7F [...] This floor captures the playful “chaos” that makes Shibuya’s Donki so famous. It is filled with everything from popular character goods and party supplies to more niche items that you will not easily find elsewhere.  
   
 Main Products  
 ・Character goods (Sanrio, Pokémon, etc.)  
 ・Cosplay supplies, party goods  
 ・Kitchenware, cookware, bath supplies, laundry supplies  
 ・Adult novelty goods, TENGA SHOP

Donki Master's TIPS [...] Q5. I want to buy souvenirs. Which floors do you recommend?
:   A5. Snacks (including Kit Kat): second floor. Cosmetics and face masks: third floor. Character goods and funny socks: fifth floor. Sake and whisky: B1F. Japan-style crafts and keychains: seventh floor.

Q6. Where are the restrooms?
:   A6. The restrooms are on the second floor. The store is large and they can be hard to find from other floors, so it is a good idea to go when you pass through the second floor.

results.title: Mega Don Quijote Shibuya Honten Store | The Official Tokyo Travel Guide, GO TOKYO
results.content:
The upper floors present a lively selection of character goods, cosplay items, and party supplies. The colorful displays attract visitors who enjoy browsing and taking photos, and simply walking through the space conveys the energetic atmosphere of Shibuya. [...] ## Floor Guide to Don Quijote Shibuya

MEGA Don Quijote Shibuya Honten Store is a multi-level shopping space where the atmosphere changes from floor to floor. With the in-store floor guide, visitors can easily see what is available from the basement to the upper levels. By exploring both the Honten Store and the Annex, shoppers can discover products from across Japan while staying in Shibuya.

### Honten Store [...] MEGA Don Quijote Shibuya Honten Store is a large discount store located near Shibuya Scramble Crossing. While there are larger Don Quijote branches elsewhere in Tokyo, this Honten Store is still among the largest. Spanning from basement level 1 to the 7th floor, it offers a wide range of products, including trending cosmetics, matcha sweets, Japanese snacks, seasonal fruits, and its popular roasted sweet potatoes.
